Subject: Throughput signal windowing & token-velocity follow-up — Cartly pilot

Hi Anya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of the performance/SLO items we discussed and the asks we need from your side to size the pilot: 

1) Traffic profile we're missing (please attach):
   - Typical request token count (avg / 50th / 95th / max).
   - Typical response token count distribution (avg / p95).
   - Requests-per-second baseline and peak windows (please specify windows: 1m, 5m, 1h).
   - Any known pre-warming/cold-start patterns (time of day, cron jobs).

2) SLO targets you expect to hit in production:
   - Latency target(s): P50 / P95 / P99 (streaming vs non-streaming).
   - Availability target and acceptable error budget.

3) Concurrency / streaming requirement:
   - Are responses streamed token-by-token, or do you aggregate and return batches?
   - Max concurrent open streams per user/session (if applicable).

4) Desired pilot constraints:
   - Target max sustained tokens/sec and observed crest QPS during peak minutes.
   - Any hard limits (cost ceiling / region / data residency).

Attached is a lightweight template (cartly_traffic_sample.csv) and a draft SLO matrix (slo_matrix_draft.xlsx) — please fill in the sample CSV with a representative 24–72 hour slice if possible. If you can provide even a CSV with timestamp, request_tokens, response_tokens, and request_type (streaming|sync), that will let us compute tokens/sec and effective QPS windows.

Next steps: if you can drop the CSV and any existing telemetry into the Drive link in this thread by EOD Thu (Jun 24), I’ll loop in Marissa and Karthik with initial sizing estimates and propose a 2-week pilot config. Also suggest a short follow-up call (30 min) this week if any of the fields above need clarification.

Thanks,
Jasmine

Hi Jasmine — thanks for the clear checklist. I attached a 48-hour slice from our production telemetry and filled the SLO draft as best we have today. A few notes inline: 

- request_tokens: median ~ 60, p95 ~ 420, occasional peaks ~ 1200 when customers submit long product descriptions.
- response_tokens: median ~ 80, p95 ~ 500.
- baseline QPS (1h rolling) ~ 12 qps, typical midday crest windows hitting 110 qps for 3–7 minutes, and rare spikes to ~220 qps for <1 minute during batch ingestion.
- about 15% of requests use streaming (real-time assistant UI), those have open streams for ~2–8s on avg.
- cold-starts: nightly maintenance jobs cause a short warm-up window at 03:00 UTC where latency jumps 2x for ~10 minutes.

We attached cartly_traffic_sample.csv (48h) and a short engineer note (attached inline) describing how we mark streaming requests. We are aiming for a P95 latency <= 400ms for interactive flows and P95 <= 1s for generative batch flows. Availability target is 99.9%.

Let me know if you need any additional fields. Happy to hop on a call Thu or Fri morning PST.

Best,
Anya

Jasmine — thanks for the forward and the sample. Quick sizing read and recommended next steps below (high-level; we can refine with model details/quantization).

1) Workload synthesis (from Cartly 48h sample):
   - Effective average tokens/sec across 48h (all requests): ~720 tokens/sec (~12 qps * 60 tokens avg).
   - Crest window observed: 110 qps with avg request tokens ~220 => crest tokens/sec ~24,200 during 3–7 minute windows.
   - Micro-spike short crests: 220 qps * avg 300 tokens => ~66k tokens/sec for <1 minute events (these are rare but must be circuit-protected).

2) Recommended pilot capacity (conservative):
   - Baseline: provision for sustained 1k tokens/sec (covers baseline + headroom for growth).
   - Burst slot pool: ability to absorb up to 30k tokens/sec for 5–10 minutes (autoscale / burst policy).
   - Emergency headroom: fallback queue/backpressure above 60k tokens/sec with graceful degradation (lower-res model variant).

3) Latency feasibility:
   - For interactive P95 <= 400ms on streaming flows, we recommend:
     * Dedicated instances with low-latency kernel path + KV cache for repeated prompts.
     * Target concurrency budget: allow ~150 simultaneous open streams (estimate from 15% streaming of crest qps).
   - If they want strict 400ms p95 under crest windows, we'll need to pin to dedicated capacity; hosted burst alone is risky.

4) Operational controls / mitigations:
   - Prefix/KV caching for common prompts to reduce average tokens generated.
   - Token-based rate limits by API key and bucketed QPS windows (1m/5m) to protect tail latency.
   - Canary pilot with a 2-week baseline where we collect live tail latency and adjust autoscale curves.

5) Proposed immediate next steps (this week):
   - SE sizing call with Cartly + Karthik (30m) to confirm model family, quantization tolerance, and streaming semantics.
   - Draft pilot config (I will produce a one-page sizing note PDF) for cost/backstop approval.

I attached a short sizing note (redwood_sizing_notes.pdf) with the math. Karthik — tagging you to confirm the concurrency calc and whether a 150 open stream budget is conservative enough or too high.

If Cartly agrees, I'll send a pilot proposal and schedule the SE call (I can do Thu 10:00–11:00 PST or Fri 09:00–10:00 PST).

-Marissa
